references.text: The Egyptians imposed forced labor on the Israelites and made their lives bitter with hard work, which is the background for Pharaoh's strategy to burden them further.
Pharaoh accuses Moses and Aaron of distracting the people from their work, leading to his decision to make the labor heavier.
Pharaoh repeats the accusation of 'false words' and orders that the workload remain unchanged without straw, implementing verse 9.
The Israelites could not listen to Moses because of discouragement and hard labor (עֲבֹדָה קָשָׁה), which resulted from Pharaoh's strategy.
The words 'דִּבְרֵי־שָׁקֶר' (false words) have a parallel in Proverbs, which warns against deceitful speech and lies.
Isaiah uses similar expressions about speaking falsehoods (דַּבֶּר־שֶׁקֶר), reflecting the biblical condemnation of lying words.
Jeremiah warns against trusting 'false words' (דִּבְרֵי הַשֶּׁקֶר), the same expression Pharaoh uses to reject Moses' message.
Direct continuation of the same event: the strategy in verse 9 is carried out concretely in verse 18.
